documents.passwordRule: First four letters of the resident's name as printed on the Aadhaar, in CAPITALS, followed by the four-digit birth year (YYYY). Spaces are skipped when counting letters; punctuation is kept (UIDAI example: P. KUMAR, born 1990 gives P.KU1990). Short names are not padded: UIDAI's example RIA, born 1990, gives RIA1990 (one blog says use the full name for names under four letters, which conflicts). Full date of birth is not used. The rule is fixed by UIDAI and cannot be changed.

sources.quote: Aadhaar card PDF password format (first four letters of name in caps followed by birth year)

documents.document: SBI account statement (bank account, not credit card)
documents.passwordRule: Conflicting by channel. Official SBI page (search snippet from sbi.co.in, not fetched): an emailed e-statement requested by SMS (ESTMT <account no.>) is encrypted with a 4-digit code the customer chooses at the time. Blogs claim other rules for net banking, mobile or branch statements: 11-digit account number; last 5 digits of registered mobile followed by DDMMYY; first 4 letters of name in caps plus DDMM; or customer ID. Not confirmed; the rule depends on how the statement was requested. Check the email or download-screen hint.

documents.document: CAMS mutual fund Consolidated Account Statement (CAS, requested on CAMS)
documents.passwordRule: Not a fixed rule: the password is the custom one you set when you request the statement on CAMS. CAMS says the statement is encrypted with that password and emailed only to the folio's registered email. Rules on the request form: alphanumeric, starts with an alphabet, 8 to 15 characters, at least one uppercase letter, at least one digit, and at least one of @ # $ * _. Blogs claim PAN in capitals or DDMMYYYY date of birth for auto-emailed statements; these are unconfirmed.

sources.quote: (fetched page had only its title; rules taken from search summary of CAMS request pages) The statement will be encrypted using the password provided by you in the form above
